description: In less than two centuries, the Aztecs built a capital of 200,000 inhabitants on a lake. Their empire, founded on tribute and sacrifice, collapsed in two years against the Spaniards.

hero.hook: A city on the water, more populated than London. Then, in two years, nothing.

blocks.text: In the heart of present-day Mexico, the Aztecs built a capital on a lake in less than two centuries, populated by **200,000 inhabitants**. Larger than London or Rome at the same time. Their power combines hydraulic engineering, demanding religion and permanent war.
Between **1519** and **1521**, this empire collapsed. Not only under the cannons of Cortés, the Spanish conquistador, but under the hatred of his subjects and under an invisible weapon: disease.

The **Mexico**, the people we will call Aztecs, come from the mythical , a place of origin to the north. They arrived in the 13th century in the Valley of Mexico. Despised, they seek a sign from their god , god of the sun and war: an eagle devouring a snake on a cactus. In **1325**, they find it on an islet in Lake **Texcoco**.  is born, their future capital. [[Aztlán]] [[Huitzilopochtli]] [[Tenochtitlán and Mexico City]]

To feed the city, they are perfecting the [[The chinampas]], ultra-fertile artificial islands made of mud and plants. Three causeways, dikes, canals: the city becomes a lake fortress and a giant market.
The Aztecs did not use the wheel for transportation and had no beasts of burden. Yet they moved millions of tons of stone for their pyramids.

sections.title: From swamps to a capital on water

blocks.text: In **1428**, Tenochtitlán allied itself with two neighboring cities, Texcoco and Tlacopan: the **Triple Alliance**. Soon, the Mexica dominate alone. Their empire does not assimilate: it demands a regular **tribute**, corn, cocoa, feathers, metals. The wealth of the capital fuels the hatred of subjugated peoples, like the [[Tlaxcaltecs]], fierce enemies of the Aztecs.

blocks.caption: Tenochtitlán, lake metropolis at the heart of the Aztec empire.

blocks.text: It is a war machine that needs perpetual conquests. When the Spaniards arrive, they will only have to unite these resentments.
Cocoa beans were used as currency. In Tenochtitlán, a rabbit was worth ten beans; a slave of good constitution, about a hundred.

sections.title: The Triple Alliance and the tribute

blocks.text: According to the [[Cosmogony of the Five Suns]], an Aztec myth, the sun only survives if it is nourished by human blood. At, the great pyramid in the center, sacrifices are not gratuitous cruelty: they are, for the Aztecs, a necessity for the world to continue. [[Templo Mayor]]

In **1519**, **Hernán Cortés** arrived with a few hundred Spaniards. , the Aztec emperor, hesitates. Steel, guns and horses are scary. But the main killer is , a European disease against which populations have no immunity. Cortés besieges the capital with thousands of indigenous allies. [[Moctezuma II]] [[Smallpox]]

events.title: Fall of Tenochtitlán

blocks.text: In **1521**, after **80 days** of siege, Tenochtitlán fell. Hungry, deprived of water, ravaged by disease. Its stones were used to build Mexico City, capital of , the Spanish colony. [[New Spain]]

Not everything disappears. The [[The chinampas]] still exist., the language of the Aztecs, is spoken by more than a million people. The eagle and the serpent remain the emblem of Mexico. A brilliant civilization survives in memory and landscape. [[Nahuatl]]

The Aztecs built a metropolis of **200, 000** inhabitants on a lake. Their tribute system and the [[Smallpox]] allowed a few hundred Spaniards, aided by local allies, to destroy the empire in two years.
